tools.name: list_tickets
tools.title: List tickets
tools.description: List tickets in recency order, optionally filtered by status, priority or last-updated time. Returns compact summaries with a short preview, not full conversation history. Freshdesk only returns tickets updated in the last 30 days unless updated_since is set — pass it explicitly for anything older. Use this to scan a queue; use get_ticket_thread once you have narrowed to a specific ticket.

updated_since.description: ISO-8601, any offset (e.g. +05:30). Only tickets updated at or after this instant.

cursor.description: Page cursor from a previous call's next_cursor. Omit for the first page. Reuse the same limit and updated_since with it, or pages will overlap or skip.

fields.description: Return only these fields of each ticket (e.g. ['id','subject','status']). Use it when scanning many tickets: it cuts the response several-fold.

tools.name: search_tickets
tools.title: Search tickets
tools.description: Server-side search across the whole helpdesk by status, priority, tag, type or creation window. Prefer this over list_tickets when you know what you are looking for. Freshdesk's search index caps results at roughly 300 (30 per page, 10 pages) and does not do free-text search over message bodies — narrow with filters, do not paginate hoping for more.

created_after.description: ISO-8601. Freshdesk search filters by calendar date, so the time of day is dropped.

tools.name: get_ticket_thread
tools.title: Get one ticket with its conversation
tools.description: Fetch a single ticket with its message thread, oldest first, as plain text. Returns the most recent max_messages messages; thread_complete tells you whether older messages exist beyond what is returned. This is the expensive call — use it on the handful of tickets you have already narrowed to. A busy thread can exceed the response budget: lower max_messages or max_chars_per_message if the result is capped.

include_contact.description: Leave ticket and message text unredacted (emails, UPI ids, phone numbers — and any card/PAN/Aadhaar-shaped strings the customer typed). It does not fetch the contact record. Only set this when the task genuinely needs it; it puts customer PII into the model's context and is logged.

tools.name: add_private_note
tools.title: Add an internal note
tools.description: Attach an internal note to a ticket. The customer never sees it. This is the agent's default way to record a finding, a draft reply for a human to send, or a recommended action. Idempotent within a connector process: re-sending a call that already succeeded with the same idempotency_key and ticket_id returns the cached result (replayed: true) instead of posting again.

idempotency_key.description: Stable key for this logical note, e.g. 'triage-<ticket_id>-<run_id>'.

tools.name: update_ticket
tools.title: Update ticket state
tools.description: Change a ticket's status, priority or tags. This is visible in the merchant's helpdesk and in their SLA reporting, so it is gated on human approval by default. It cannot author anything to the customer — there is no tool in this connector that can — but resolving or closing a ticket may trigger the merchant's own Freshdesk notifications and automations. add_tags merges with the ticket's existing tags; it never removes any.

reason.description: Why this change is correct. Written to the audit log and shown to the approver.
